Extract known kin within generation-distance bounds

Source: R/extract_kin.R
extract_kin.Rd

Extract kin of a set of ego individuals from simulated data. Kin relations are governed by generational distance.

Usage

extract_kin(population, ego_ids, generations = 2, relative_ids = NULL)

Arguments

population

A hammel_population with a finite end_time.

ego_ids

Unique person IDs whose known kin should be extracted.

generations

Nonnegative whole number of parent generations on EACH side, default 2. Zero returns no kin between distinct people.

relative_ids

Optional unique relative IDs to consider. NULL means all recorded persons. Unknown IDs are errors; empty vectors return no rows.

Value

A tibble with one row per ego and relative: ego_id, relative_id, relationship, ego_distance, relative_distance, n_common_ancestors, ego_lineage, relative_lineage, ego_ancestry_complete, and relative_ancestry_complete. Lineage is "self", "maternal", "paternal", or "both" for shortest routes to the closest common ancestors.

Details

Find recorded common ancestors within generations parent steps of both an ego and a relative, including each person at distance zero. This function uses the same native kinship module as union eligibility. Unknown parents terminate their branches. At depth two, known parents/children, grandparents/grandchildren, siblings, aunts/uncles, nieces/nephews, and first cousins are included, including half relationships. Great-grandparents and first cousins once removed require depth three.

Returns one row per relative, describing their closest common ancestors: those with the smallest sum of the two distances within the requested bounds. n_common_ancestors counts them, ordinarily 2 for full kin and 1 for half kin; a count of 1 is only recorded evidence when a parent is unknown. relationship names the distance pair, such as "sibling", "aunt_uncle" or "first_cousin", with full and half kin together. The ego itself is excluded. Includes deceased and living people in recorded history; use count_kin() for mean counts of living kin at given times.

See also

count_kin()

Examples

population <- generate_uniform_population(1000)
model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_population(population) |>
  set_mortality(usa_2000_mortality) |>
  set_fertility(usa_2000_fertility) |>
  set_union_formation(
    "on_demand",
    matching = age_gap_matching_model(3, 5)
  )
result <- run_simulation(model, years = 50, seed = 42)
extract_kin(result, max(result$persons$person_id))
